node.title: From Frontier Engineering to Ecosystem Awareness — Twenty Years of Architectural Continuity
node.reading:
GEPLAN, airport transformation, xSeil and Phylons belong to different operating worlds. Their common thread is a practical architectural problem: a decision depends on information, resources, relationships and assumptions that can change while the system is running. Twenty years of work across those environments gave that problem concrete form. Current research makes its recurring structure explicit and reusable.

Historical projects supply engineering evidence. Research develops models and interfaces from that experience; pre-standardization work exposes those proposals to wider technical discussion.

relations: Cross-frontier activation can also run from field constraints to research questions, provided later formalization is kept separate from validation of the original cases.
Linaje compartido y continuidad intelectual no equivalen a evidencia experimental independiente.
The field histories can inform the later two-origin research formulation while retaining their individual dates, domains and evidential responsibilities.
La influencia es declarada por autores del mismo corpus; no constituye corroboración independiente.
The conceptual lineage map can make the transition from field mechanism to research question inspectable without turning continuity into independent validation.
La genealogía del propio corpus no verifica por sí sola prioridad, novedad o rendimiento del método.
